newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong store jacks up price of Deng watch.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong store jacks up price of Deng watch.

text.p: A Hong Kong company selling a watch featuring the late Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping waving his arm has jacked up the price of the timepiece by over 50 percent since Deng died last week.
"The price was raised mainly because we believe it is a commemorative item and is worth more," Vicky Wong, a marketing officer at Tang's Department Stores Ltd, told Reuters on Monday.
She said the novelty watch, then priced at HK$390 ($50), sold out when rumours broke last week that 92-year-old Deng was fading. He died on Wednesday night.
When stocks were replenished, Wong added, the price would be hiked to HK$590 (US$76).
The watch shows on its face the smiling paramount Chinese leader dressed in the drills of the People's Liberation Army, his arm waving back and forth.
There has been a rush to buy Deng memorabilia in the British colony, which China is set to take back on July 1 under a "one country two systems" policy designed by Deng. ($1=HK$7.8)
